title: Integrated analysis of single-cell and bulk RNA-seq reveals MAGEA3/6-associated immune subtypes and key immune genes in gastric cancer
subjects: /Biology and life sciences/Cell biology/Cellular types/Animal cells/Epithelial cells
/Biology and life sciences/Cell biology/Cellular types/Animal cells/Immune cells
/Medicine and health sciences/Clinical medicine/Clinical immunology/Immunotherapy/Cancer immunotherapy

figures.label: Fig 1
figures.caption: Identification of epithelial cells and epithelial differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in gastric tissues.(A) Principal component analysis (PCA) and graph-based clustering of single-cell RNA sequencing data identified eight distinct cell clusters. (B) Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) plot showing annotated cell types based on canonical marker genes. (C) Expression of canonical marker genes used for cell type identification. (D) Venn diagram showing the intersection of DEGs between tumor vs. normal epithelial cells and TCGA-STAD dataset, resulting in 23 epithelial DEGs.

figures.label: Fig 2
figures.caption: Identification of epithelial-related DEGs associated with immune infiltration.(A) Correlation analysis between 23 epithelial-related DEGs and immune scores calculated using the ESTIMATE algorithm; MAGEA3 and MAGEA6 show strongest correlations. (B) Boxplots comparing MAGEA3 and MAGEA6 expression between tumor and adjacent normal tissues in TCGA-STAD. (C) Consensus clustering of 410 TCGA-STAD samples based on MAGEA3 and MAGEA6 expression, revealing two molecular subtypes. (D) Expression levels of MAGEA3 and MAGEA6 in Group 1 (high expression) and Group 2 (low expression). (E) Spearman correlation analysis between MAGEA3 and MAGEA6 expression levels.

figures.label: Fig 3
figures.caption: Functional enrichment analysis of DEGs between Group 1 and Group 2.(A) Heatmap of DEGs shows clear separation between Group 1 and Group 2. (B) Volcano plot of DEGs between Group 1 and Group 2. (C) GO enrichment analysis of DEGs. (D) KEGG pathway analysis of DEGs. (E) Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) of Hallmark gene sets showing enrichment of immune/inflammatory pathways.

figures.label: Fig 4
figures.caption: Comparison of immune infiltration between the two molecular subtypes.(A) CIBERSORT analysis showing relative immune cell proportions. (B) ssGSEA scores of 28 immune cell types. (C) ESTIMATE-derived stromal, immune, and ESTIMATE scores. (D) Xcell analysis of 64 immune cell types.

figures.label: Fig 5
figures.caption: Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identifies immune-related gene modules.(A) Analysis of network topology for soft powers. (B) Gene dendrogram and module colors. (C-D) Correlation between module eigengenes and immune traits. (E) GO enrichment analysis of yellow module genes. (F) KEGG pathway analysis of yellow module genes.

figures.label: Fig 6
figures.caption: Clinical significance and mutation profiles of molecular subtypes.(A) Survival analysis of 2 groups. (B) Forest plot from Cox regression analysis identifying CTLA4, TAP1, BCL11B, and PAEP. (C) Boxplots comparing expression of CTLA4, TAP1, BCL11B and PAEP between Group 1 and Group 2. (D) Correlation analysis of MAGEA3/6 with BCL11B and PAEP expression.

figures.label: Fig 7
figures.caption: Immune infiltration analysis based on BCL11B expression levels.(A) CIBERSORT analysis showing relative immune cell proportions. (B) ssGSEA scores of 28 immune cell types. (C) ESTIMATE-derived stromal, immune, and ESTIMATE scores. (D) Xcell analysis of 64 immune cell types.

figures.label: Fig 8
figures.caption: Immune infiltration analysis based on PAEP expression levels.(A) CIBERSORT analysis showing relative immune cell proportions. (B) ssGSEA scores of 28 immune cell types. (C) ESTIMATE-derived stromal, immune, and ESTIMATE scores. (D) Xcell analysis of 64 immune cell types.
